item.title: Korea President’s Stock Dream Bumps Into Leveraged ETF Backlash
item.description: South Korea’s most closely watched stock-market innovation is morphing into a headache for President Lee Jae Myung.

item.title: Aussie’s Slide Versus Kiwi to Slow on Rate Gap, Strategists Say
item.description: The Australian dollar’s steep selloff against its New Zealand counterpart is set to slow, with analysts saying Australia’s higher interest rates and a key technical support will cushion the currency.

item.title: Bond Traders Take Warsh at Word, See Inflation Fight Continuing
item.description: Bond traders and Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh are in agreement on a crucial point: The central bank’s fight against inflation still seems far from over.

item.title: Tropical Storm Watches Posted Across Florida’s Panhandle Region
item.description: A tropical storm watch has been issued for the Florida Panhandle as the Atlantic’s next event takes shape off shore.

item.title: Why Apple’s OpenAI Lawsuit Doesn’t Mention Jony Ive; AI Recording at Genius Bar
item.description: Also: The company tries out AI recording for Genius Bar appointments.

item.title: Extreme Stock Swings Tempt Funds Into Reverse Dispersion Trade
item.description: Betting that individual stocks will be volatile while the S&P 500 stays relatively calm has been a popular and successful hedge fund strategy. But with the swings in share prices reaching extreme levels, the reverse trade is gaining traction with investors.

item.title: Prediction Markets Swell to 27% of Sports Bets During World Cup
item.description: Prediction-market trading has surged during a blowout World Cup, far outpacing the growth at traditional sportsbooks and driving home the competitive threat that companies like Kalshi now pose to the sports-gambling industry.

item.title: Big Tech Needs to Justify AI Spending as Investors Dump Stocks
item.description: After last week’s wipeout in chips and the broader selloff in technology stocks, pressure is building for the biggest spenders on artificial intelligence to justify their expenditures to beleaguered traders with increasingly itchy fingers hovering over their sell buttons.

item.title: Safest Carry in Emerging Markets Is in Latin American Currencies
item.description: Emerging-market currency volatility has dropped to the lowest since the start of year and that’s re-energizing carry trades, particularly those involving Latin America that are seen to offer the juiciest returns.

item.title: Clear Skies Now Expected for World Cup Final in New Jersey
item.description: Clear skies are expected across northern New Jersey as the World Cup final between Argentina and Spain is set to get underway at MetLife Stadium on Sunday afternoon with about 80,000 fans on hand.

item.title: Alibaba’s Qwen Unveils Preview of Flagship AI Model
item.description: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. launched a preview version of its flagship Qwen3.8 Max model, which it described as comparable to leading frontier AI models and second only to Anthropic PBC’s Fable 5.

item.title: Shakira’s Tax Fight in Spain Puts Agency Bonuses Under Scrutiny
item.description: Shakira thought she’d won. After a judge in April wiped out €55 million ($63 million) in tax claims against her, the singer dedicated her victory to “ordinary citizens who are abused and crushed every day by a system that presumes their guilt.”

item.title: Caspian Pipeline Consortium Halts Loadings After Drone Strike
item.description: Oil loading at the Caspian Pipeline Consortium’s terminal on Russia’s Black Sea coast was halted after a drone strike.

item.title: US, Iran Trade More Attacks After Two Troops Killed in Jordan
item.description: The US and Iran engaged in another wave of tit-for-tat attacks, signaling no let-up after strikes by the Islamic Republic killed two American service members in Jordan on Friday.

item.title: China’s Moonshot Plans IPO in Six Months After AI Breakthrough
item.description: Moonshot AI has told investors it’s preparing to list in as early as six months, seizing the opportunity to tap capital markets after its latest model upended industry perceptions of China’s burgeoning capabilities and sent global tech stocks reeling.

item.title: India’s Private Lenders Bet on Corporate Loan Revival for Growth
item.description: India’s top private banks are betting on a sustained pick up in lending after reporting healthy numbers in the first quarter of the fiscal year, as more companies shift away from pricier bond market borrowings to cheaper loans.

item.title: Jingye Says It Reserves Legal Rights in UK Steel Nationalization
item.description: Jingye Steel Co. has reserved all legal rights, including international arbitration, over the UK government’s nationalization of British Steel.

item.title: Singapore Weighs Hedge Fund Tax Cuts to Be More Competitive: FT
item.description: The Monetary Authority of Singapore has held talks with investment firms on reducing taxes for fund managers in a bid to maintain the island’s competitiveness and retain talent, the Financial Times reported.

item.title: South Korea to Ease FX Rules for Foreigners to Trade Won Easier
item.description: South Korea laid out a detailed plan to make the won freely tradable among foreigners, its boldest step yet to liberalize the forex market and bring the currency closer to full convertibility.

item.title: Venezuela’s Official Earthquake Death Toll Rises to 5,119
item.description: The official death toll from the twin earthquakes that struck Venezuela last month rose to 5,119, according to National Assembly head Jorge Rodríguez.

item.title: Korea’s AI-Heavy Market Now Sets the Tone for Global Stocks
item.description: For fund managers in London, New York and Tokyo, a new ritual has emerged before trading gets underway: checking South Korean stocks.

item.title: ECB Expected to Skip Rate Hike, Keep September Option Open
item.description: The European Central Bank is likely to hold off on a second interest-rate hike in the coming week while keeping that option open for September.

item.title: Vanishing CLO Profits Are Sparking Infighting: Credit Weekly
item.description: A type of investment that once generated some of Wall Street’s juiciest fixed-income returns has deteriorated so badly that investors are heading for the exits and arguing about who’s to blame.

item.title: Chinese Trucks Pose New Peril in Mexico’s US Tariff Relief Bid
item.description: Mexico’s growing fleet of Chinese-made heavy trucks is becoming a new obstacle in its quest for relief from US tariffs, as Washington presses for assurances that its southern neighbor isn’t becoming a backdoor for Chinese manufacturers to enter North America.

item.title: Warsh Shows His Inner Hawk as Inflation Debate Heats Up
item.description: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh hammered home the message this week that the US central bank is on inflation watch. The test to deliver on that promise could come soon.

item.title: Kerala Aims to Attract $1 Billion In Shipbuilding From Investors
item.description: The Kerala Government on Saturday clarified that the southern Indian state aims to attract 100 billion rupees ($1 billion) of investment in shipbuilding from multiple investors, rather than a single source, in the coming years.

item.title: Oil’s Battered Shock Absorbers Risk Price Spike as War Returns
item.description: Global oil markets have been spared an extreme squeeze during the first phase of the Iran war, but renewed fighting is bringing with it greater risk of a price spike in a world where supply buffers have been worn perilously thin.

item.title: Zelenskyy May Fire Commander Syrskyi After Protests, FT Reports
item.description: Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is considering firing Armed Forces commander-in-chief Oleksandr Syrskyi, the Financial Times reported, following days of turmoil engulfing the country’s military leadership.

item.title: Not Done Yet Refunding Tariffs or Realizing AI’s Promise
item.description: The markets continue to be dominated by news of artificial intelligence

item.title: Moonshot’s Kimi Upends Conventional Wisdom on US Lead Over China
item.description: At an event in Beijing earlier this year, some of China’s top artificial intelligence leaders warned that the country remained meaningfully behind the US in developing cutting-edge AI models, with one executive arguing that “the gap may actually be widening.”
